bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Going concern uncertainty flagged by statutory auditors — Statutory Auditors drew attention to delays in realization of receivables, resulting in temporary liquidity constraints and related concerns regarding the Company's ability to continue as a going concern; management attributes this to delayed realization of receivables from Government departments and Government-backed authorities.
- Concentration in Government and Government-backed customers — The Company's receivables and revenue realization depend heavily on certification and payment releases from Government departments and Government-backed authorities, and delays in this process directly caused the FY2026 liquidity constraints.
- Contract termination and litigation exposure — The Jaipur–Sawai Madhopur Doubling Project contract was rescinded by North Western Railway (termination notice dated January 13, 2026) with encashment of performance bank guarantee and forfeiture of security deposit; the Company has challenged this before the Rajasthan High Court, Jodhpur, and the matter is pending adjudication. Separately, the VPRPL-KSIPL BKN JV contract for the Bikaner Railway Station EPC project was terminated, with a consequential order for encashment of bank guarantee and forfeiture of security deposit, also under challenge before the Rajasthan High Court, Jodhpur, and pending.
- Delay in payment of statutory dues — Statutory Auditors reported delays in deposit of GST, Provident Fund and ESI dues in certain cases, and delays in payment of Income Tax and TDS, attributable to temporary liquidity constraints arising from delayed realization of receivables; the Company is taking steps to discharge these dues along with applicable interest.
- Reliance on continued Promoter financial support — The Board's going-concern assessment relies partly on continued Promoter support through unsecured, interest-free loans, alongside projected cash flows and expected realization of receivables and claims.

outlook.body:
- Focus on restoring execution momentum and converting the existing order book into billed revenue and collections in FY2027.
- Clear pending work certifications and realise long-standing receivables from government departments before pursuing growth.
- Manage working capital with discipline; keep new tendering selective until liquidity conditions normalise.
- Continue leveraging in-house EPC capabilities and equipment fleet to control cost and delivery.
- Pursue opportunities under Jal Jeevan Mission 2.0 and AMRUT 2.0, alongside continued participation in railway and road infrastructure.
- Bid selectively going forward, in segments and geographies where the Company has executed before and where payment behaviour is proven.
- Sequence FY2027 priorities: clear the certification backlog, convert certified work into billing, convert billing into collection, and only then return to order-book growth.
- Evaluate new business opportunities selectively, prioritising projects offering sustainable returns, manageable risks, and strong alignment with technical expertise and execution capabilities.
- Maintain a prudent balance between growth, risk and capital deployment while building a diversified, high-quality project portfolio.
- Place strong emphasis on execution excellence, quality, safety, timely delivery and customer satisfaction to scale operations responsibly.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: VPRPL's growth plans are execution-led rather than asset/capacity-led: the Company operates an integrated EPC business model (no owned plants or manufacturing capacity disclosed) and expects to expand its footprint through selective bidding under Jal Jeevan Mission 2.0 (approved March 2026, outlay ₹8.69 lakh crore to December 2028) and AMRUT 2.0, alongside continued participation in railway and road infrastructure. The Company maintains a fleet of approximately 500 pieces of construction equipment supporting in-house design, procurement, and execution, and plans to continue leveraging this integrated model and equipment fleet to control cost and delivery rather than pursue new asset-heavy capacity.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Central funding under the Jal Jeevan Mission fell sharply (to ₹22,670 crore in 2024-25 from ₹70,000 crore the prior year) as the Mission approached the end of its first phase, slowing certification and payment releases across the Company's principal markets.
- The approval of Jal Jeevan Mission 2.0 in March 2026, with a total outlay of ₹8.69 lakh crore (including central assistance of ₹3.59 lakh crore) extending the Mission to December 2028, reopens and expands the principal programme pipeline the Company serves — restoring programme funding that was absent through FY2026.
- JJM 2.0 restructures the Mission from infrastructure creation to service delivery, with villages certified under a national digital framework and Har Ghar Jal declared only once adequate in-village O&M arrangements are in place — a shift management says favours VPRPL's combined construction-plus-O&M contract model, which does not rely on HAM or BOT concessions.
- AMRUT 2.0 continues with an indicative outlay of ₹2,99,000 crore for universal urban water supply and sewerage coverage; the railway budget stands at ₹2.78 lakh crore for 2026-27; India's metro network has grown from 248 km across five cities in 2014 to 1,095 km across twenty-six — markets the Company is qualified in and has executed in.
- Public capital expenditure has been raised to ₹12.2 lakh crore for FY2026-27 from ₹11.2 lakh crore, continuing a decade-long rise, and the Union Budget has proposed an Infrastructure Risk Guarantee Fund addressing construction-phase risk.
- The Reserve Bank projects real GDP growth of 6.6% for 2026-27 with the policy repo rate held at 5.25% (neutral stance); the revised Index of Core Industries grew 5.0% in June 2026, led by iron ore, electricity, cement and steel.
- The portfolio remains diversified across water supply, railway, and road and civil segments, reducing dependence on any single sector.
- The proximate cause of FY2026's deterioration was working capital, with the root cause being certification: the build-certify-bill-collect cycle stalled when certification slowed, while cost continued to accrue; collection days extended from 204 to 277 and inventory days from 209 to 305 during the year.
- Order book stood at approximately ₹43,910.9 million as of March 2026, providing revenue visibility for approximately 2-3 years.
- The Company was awarded a total of three new projects during the financial year, with a cumulative bid project cost of ₹1,148.1 million.
- The Company successfully completed six projects during the period under review, totalling ₹3,628.7 million in value.
- The order book spans water supply, railway, and road and civil projects across eleven states.

deepdive.thesis: Vishnu Prakash R Punglia Limited is a construction company with a strong order book, but faces challenges in executing projects and managing working capital, leading to a negative credit rating outlook.

open.item: For FY2027, priorities are narrow and sequenced: clear the certification backlog, convert certified work into billing, convert billing into collection, and only then return to growth in the order book, while continuing to bid selectively in proven segments and geographies.

VPRPL will continue to leverage its in-house EPC capabilities and equipment fleet to control cost and delivery and will pursue opportunities under Jal Jeevan Mission 2.0 and AMRUT 2.0, alongside continued participation in railway and road infrastructure.

In FY2027, VPRPL will focus on restoring execution momentum and converting its existing order book into billed revenue and collections, with priorities of clearing pending work certifications, realising long-standing receivables, and managing working capital with discipline.

The Board approved raising up to ₹3,000 million through equity or equity-linked instruments, intended to restore balance sheet capacity, not fund expansion, and the Company is seeking shareholder approval to increase authorised share capital to ₹2,000 million.
New tendering will remain selective until liquidity conditions normalise.
Credit rating was downgraded during the year, and the Company has engaged a new rating agency to conduct a fresh assessment of its facilities.
VPRPL will pursue opportunities under Jal Jeevan Mission 2.0 and AMRUT 2.0, alongside continued participation in railway and road infrastructure.

The Company is taking necessary steps to discharge outstanding statutory dues (GST, PF, ESI, Income Tax and TDS delays), together with applicable interest and other statutory liabilities, and is strengthening cash-flow management and statutory compliance processes.

The approval of Jal Jeevan Mission 2.0 in March 2026, with an outlay of ₹8.69 lakh crore to December 2028, reopens the principal programme pipeline the Company serves, and VPRPL will pursue opportunities under it and AMRUT 2.0.
